# NavSentinel North-Star — External Research GAP-FILL

**Focus:** A=on-device ML runtime feasibility · B=interaction-attack published rates · C=visual brand-impersonation SOTA · D=local feedback/conformal loop.

## Executive summary

For a local-first single-user Chrome MV3 security extension, the evidence is strongest on GAP A (runtime feasibility) and GAP B (interaction-level attacks), thinner on GAP C (visual phishing), and effectively absent on GAP D. GAP A: on-device ML is technically viable in an MV3 offscreen document via TensorFlow.js or ONNX-runtime-web (WebGPU default-on since Chrome 113, giving ~3.8-19x speedups over WASM), but peak inference memory can vastly exceed model-on-disk size (up to 334.6x in a worst case), and Chrome's built-in Gemini Nano carries a heavy hardware/storage bar (>4GB VRAM or 16GB RAM+4 cores, 22GB free disk, auto-removed below 10GB) that makes it opt-in and excludes many devices — so the extension must treat built-in AI as a conditional enhancement with fallback paths, host inference in an offscreen document (Prompt API does not work in service workers/Web Workers), and respect the single-offscreen-document limit. GAP B: DoubleClickjacking and ClickFix are real interaction-layer attacks that by design bypass server-side header/cookie defenses and URL-blocklist/EDR-style controls (Microsoft observed thousands of devices/month executing ClickFix commands despite EDR), quantifying a genuine gap that an interaction-monitoring extension can address. GAP C: Phishpedia (logo/Siamese-embedding based) reports 99.2% identification / 98.2% precision / 87.1% recall at 0.19s/page and far outperforms perceptual-hash and earlier baselines, while a pure on-device pHash extension (PhishSnap) demonstrates client-side feasibility but at a low accuracy floor — favoring logo-embedding over perceptual hashing for client-side use. GAP D produced zero surviving claims, so no verified guidance on conformal calibration, rrweb capture, or single-user active learning is available from this research pass.

## Confirmed findings (10)

### On-device ML inference is viable inside an MV3 offscreen document using TensorFlow.js or ONNX-runtime-web, and the WebGPU backend (default-on in Chrome since v113) gives large speedups over the WASM/CPU path — but engineers must budget for peak inference memory that can hugely exceed model-on-disk size.
- **Confidence:** high · 3-0 (merged from 4 unanimous claims)
- **Sources:** https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3688843 · https://opensource.microsoft.com/blog/2024/02/29/onnx-runtime-web-unleashes-generative-ai-in-the-browser-using-webgpu/ · https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/offscreen
- **Evidence:** TensorFlow.js and ONNX-runtime-web are the two most widely adopted browser DL runtimes (ACM TOSEM, DOI 10.1145/3688843), making them the practical baseline (CPU slowdown driven by WASM runtime inefficiency and underutilized SIMD). ONNX Runtime Web + WebGPU accelerated the Segment Anything encoder ~19x and decoder ~3.8x on an Intel i9 laptop + RTX 3060 (Microsoft primary blog). WebGPU is default-on since Chrome/Edge 113 (Mac/Win/ChromeOS) and Chrome 121 Android. MV3 hosts this off the service worker via chrome.offscreen.createDocument()/closeDocument() loading a static bundled HTML file (service workers lack DOM/WebGPU-in-SW historically; ONNX backends fail in service workers). CRITICAL BUDGET CAVEAT: in-browser inference memory can exceed 334.6x the model's on-disk size in a worst case (super-resolution / large intermediate activations) due to suboptimal memory management — a small on-disk model can still blow an offscreen-document memory budget. The 334.6x is a peak, not typical; a lightweight classifier/embedding model would be far lower, but the qualitative point (peak memory >> model size) holds.

### Only ONE offscreen document can be open per installed extension at a time (plus one for an active incognito split-mode profile), and the offscreen document must load a static bundled HTML file — constraining how many parallel inference hosts the extension can run.
- **Confidence:** high · 3-0 (merged from 2 unanimous claims)
- **Sources:** https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/offscreen
- **Evidence:** Official Chrome offscreen API docs: 'Though an extension package can contain multiple offscreen documents, an installed extension can only have one open at a time' plus one additional for an active incognito split-mode profile. The document's URL must be a static HTML file bundled with the extension; created/closed via chrome.offscreen.createDocument()/closeDocument(). This is the canonical MV3 mechanism for hosting DOM/WASM/WebGPU inference off the ephemeral service worker, but the single-document cap prevents spinning up parallel offscreen inference hosts. Offscreen API is GA since Chrome 109 (Jan 2023).

### Chrome's built-in Gemini Nano (Prompt API) imposes a heavy hardware and storage bar that makes it opt-in/gated and excludes a large fraction of typical devices: strictly more than 4GB VRAM (GPU path) OR 16GB+ RAM and 4+ CPU cores (CPU path), plus at least 22GB free disk on the Chrome profile volume, with the model auto-removed if free space drops below 10GB.
- **Confidence:** high · 3-0 / 2-1 (merged from 3 claims; the strongest hardware/storage figures are 3-0)
- **Sources:** https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/get-started · https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/prompt-api
- **Evidence:** Verbatim across two official Chrome docs: 'Strictly more than 4 GB of VRAM'; '16 GB of RAM or more and 4 CPU cores or more'; 'At least 22 GB of free space on the volume that contains your Chrome profile'; 'If the available storage space falls to less than 10 GB after the download, the model is removed.' On-disk weights are ~2-4GB (the 22GB is a free-space gate to trigger download, not model size). The audio-input variant still requires a GPU. The 'excludes a large fraction of devices' framing is a grounded inference, not a Google figure: Steam Hardware Survey (a higher-end gaming-skewed sample) shows only ~40-42% of machines with 16GB RAM as of 2025-2026, so the general population is weaker. Implication: on-device inference cannot be assumed persistent; storage cost is large for a browser extension.

### Chrome relaxed the GPU-only requirement for Gemini Nano by adding a CPU inference path on Linux/macOS/Windows starting in Chrome 140 (announced Oct 1, 2025), broadening eligible devices to those without capable GPUs.
- **Confidence:** high · 3-0 / 2-1 (merged from 2 claims)
- **Sources:** https://developer.chrome.com/blog/gemini-nano-cpu-support
- **Evidence:** Official Chrome blog 'Expanding built-in AI to more devices' (2025-10-01): 'CPU support for Gemini Nano is rolling out in Chrome 140' and 'By enabling CPU inference on Linux, macOS, and Windows, many more users can benefit...'. CPU inference requires 16GB RAM + 4 cores (+ ~22GB disk) instead of a capable GPU. Caveat: CPU inference is slower than GPU; the audio-input variant still needs a GPU; WebGPU/Wasm remains the GPU acceleration backend (the GPU REQUIREMENT relaxed, WebGPU itself was not removed).

### The Prompt API is opt-in and conditionally available — it exposes a multi-state availability check and requires user activation before the model downloads — and it does NOT run in Web Workers or (per docs) service workers, only top-level windows and same-origin iframes. An MV3 extension must therefore host Prompt-API inference in an offscreen document with explicit fallback paths.
- **Confidence:** high · 3-0 / 2-1 (merged from 2 claims)
- **Sources:** https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/prompt-api · https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/get-started
- **Evidence:** Docs: 'The Prompt API isn't available in Web Workers for now' and 'By default, the Prompt API is only available to top-level windows and to their same-origin iframes.' LanguageModel.availability() returns states (available / downloadable / downloading / unavailable — the docs actually list four, so the extension must handle more conditional paths, not fewer). Model download requires meaningful user interaction (user activation) before create(). Developer consensus (2025-2026 guides) confirms the MV3 pattern: the service worker forwards requests to an offscreen document (or page context) that calls LanguageModel.create(). Caveat: the worker constraint is explicitly 'for now' and Chrome built-in AI is fast-moving.

### Built-in Gemini Nano runs locally and works offline after a one-time model download — on-device inference with no cloud round-trip — though Google's consumer privacy WORDING softened in Chrome 148 (May 2026) and the 'no third party' guarantee carries a web-exposure caveat.
- **Confidence:** medium · 2-1
- **Sources:** https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/get-started
- **Evidence:** Docs: 'No data is sent to Google or any third party when using the model' and 'Subsequent use of the model does not require a network connection.' Corroborated by Android Authority/gHacks (runs entirely offline post-download). CAVEATS that must be reported: (1) In Chrome 148 (rolled out May 2026) Google removed the consumer-settings phrase 'without sending your data to Google servers'; a Google spokesperson said this 'doesn't reflect a change to how we handle on-device AI' and data 'is processed solely on device' — wording softened, behavior reaffirmed. (2) 'No third party' is conditional: the Prompt API exposes the model to WEBSITES, so a site invoking it sees model inputs/outputs under its own privacy policy; usage is also gated by Google's changeable Generative AI Prohibited Uses Policy. (3) Chrome's cloud 'AI Mode' is distinct from the local Prompt API and DOES route to Google servers — a common source of confusion. The local/offline runtime behavior (the decision-relevant fact for GAP A) is not refuted.

### DoubleClickjacking is a real interaction-level attack that bypasses all standard server-side clickjacking defenses (X-Frame-Options, CSP frame-ancestors, SameSite Lax/Strict cookies) by operating across separate browser windows rather than iframes — exploiting double-click event ordering.
- **Confidence:** high · 3-0 (merged from 2 unanimous claims)
- **Sources:** https://www.evil.blog/2024/12/doubleclickjacking-what.html
- **Evidence:** Paulos Yibelo's original Dec-2024 disclosure: the attack bypasses 'all known clickjacking protections, including the X-Frame-Options header, CSP's frame-ancestors and SameSite: Lax/Strict cookies' because it uses window.open() to create a separate top-level (non-framed, first-party) window. Mechanism: 'The first click (triggered on mousedown) causes the top window to close. The second click lands on the now-exposed authorization button'; the child window uses window.opener.location to retarget the parent to the target page. Corroborated by The Hacker News, Infosecurity, SecurityAffairs, BleepingComputer. Boundary nuance: JavaScript gesture-gating client-side defenses (Dropbox/Stripe/GitHub) DO stop it — which is precisely the seam a client-side interaction monitor can occupy, since the named server-side header/cookie defenses cannot.

### ClickFix (fake-CAPTCHA / clipboard-paste social engineering) operates at the interaction layer and by design bypasses conventional, automated, URL-blocklist, AND EDR controls — quantifying the detection gap left by URL-reputation-only products. Microsoft observed thousands of devices/month actually EXECUTING ClickFix commands in early 2025 despite EDR being present, with campaigns hitting thousands of devices globally per day.
- **Confidence:** high · 3-0 (merged from 3 unanimous claims)
- **Sources:** https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/08/21/think-before-you-clickfix-analyzing-the-clickfix-social-engineering-technique/
- **Evidence:** Microsoft Security blog (2025-08-21): 'Because ClickFix relies on human intervention to launch the malicious commands, a campaign that uses this technique could get past conventional and automated security solutions.' Scale: 'campaigns targeting thousands of enterprise and end-user devices globally every day.' Detection gap: 'In early 2025, Microsoft Defender Experts observed thousands of devices being affected by a ClickFix attack (that is, the ClickFix command was executed by a user on the device) per month, even with an EDR solution enabled.' Independent corroboration: ESET H1 2025 report (ClickFix/FakeCaptcha surged 517% H2-2024→H1-2025, ~8% of all blocked attacks, 2nd most common vector after phishing); Microsoft 2025 Digital Defense Report (ClickFix = 47% of initial-access attacks tracked by MDE, exceeding phishing at 35%); Group-IB (IP/URL/DNS reputation outpaced by disposable domains; user-initiated action bypasses perimeter defenses). The lure operates at the interaction layer URL reputation cannot inspect — directly the gap a client-side interaction monitor addresses.

### For visual brand-impersonation detection, logo/embedding-based methods substantially outperform perceptual-hash and earlier baselines: Phishpedia reports 99.2% identification, 98.2% precision, 87.1% recall at 0.19s/page, versus EMD (52-89% precision), PhishZoo (68.9% precision), and LogoSENSE (20.5% precision / 26.9% recall).
- **Confidence:** high · 3-0
- **Sources:** https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec21fall-lin.pdf
- **Evidence:** USENIX Security '21 (Lin et al.), Table 2 verified by direct PDF extraction: Phishpedia 99.2% identification rate / 98.2% precision / 87.1% recall / 0.19s prediction time. Baselines: EMDnormal 52.0% precision / 76.2% recall, EMDmore_ref 89.0% precision, PhishZoo 68.9% precision / 81.8% recall (18.2s), LogoSENSE 20.5% precision / 26.9% recall (27.2s). Phishpedia identifies spoofed brand login pages via logo recognition + Siamese-style brand matching against a reference list. HONESTY CAVEAT: Phishpedia is an IDENTIFICATION system (assumes a candidate page is already flagged), not a standalone detector, and later work (PhishAgent, Liu 2024 reference-free) critiques its limited BRAND COVERAGE in the wild — but the reported benchmark metrics stand. This favors logo-embedding over perceptual hashing for the accuracy ceiling.

### A pure on-device perceptual-hashing approach (PhishSnap) demonstrates fully client-side visual phishing detection is feasible in a browser extension with zero network calls — using a 64-bit pHash (32x32 resize + DCT, low-frequency 8x8 coefficients, Hamming distance against brand templates) — but at a low accuracy floor that confirms pHash is the weak/evadable option versus logo-CNN/Siamese embeddings.
- **Confidence:** high · 3-0
- **Sources:** https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02243v1
- **Evidence:** PhishSnap (arXiv 2512.02243v1, submitted 2025-12-01): 'All logic executes locally, ensuring that no screenshots or hashes leave the device' and 'no network requests are made.' Mechanism: resize to 32x32, DCT, extract low-frequency 8x8 coefficients, convert to bits → 64-bit hash, compare via Hamming distance to legitimate templates. This proves client-side feasibility (privacy + speed). NOTE: the paper's own reported accuracy (~0.79 acc / 0.76 precision / 0.78 recall) and pHash's evadability against brandless/adaptive layouts were SEPARATELY REFUTED as standalone claims in this research pass (0-3 votes) — so treat those specific numbers as unverified — but the descriptive feasibility claim (on-device pHash works, with pHash as the weaker option) survived. The realistic accuracy floor for pure on-device perceptual hashing is therefore low; logo-embedding is preferable where it can run client-side.

## Caveats & refuted

Time-sensitivity: Chrome built-in AI (Gemini Nano / Prompt API) is fast-moving and explicitly experimental — hardware specs, availability states, the Web-Worker/service-worker constraint ('for now'), model size (~2-4GB, 'may vary with browser updates'), and even consumer privacy wording (changed in Chrome 148, May 2026) are all moving targets. Any Prompt-API-dependent design must re-verify availability() states and the offscreen-document hosting pattern at implementation time. Memory caveat: the 334.6x peak-inference-memory multiplier is a worst case (super-resolution / large intermediate activations), NOT a typical figure for a lightweight security classifier/embedding model — do not over-apply it; the qualitative point (peak memory >> on-disk size) is what generalizes. Source-strength caveats: the WebGPU 19x/3.8x speedup is a vendor (Microsoft) blog on favorable discrete-GPU hardware (RTX 3060), not representative of integrated/low-end GPUs; the 'fraction of users meeting the hardware bar' is grounded inference (Steam Hardware Survey, gaming-skewed) not a Google-published figure; ClickFix 'thousands daily/monthly' are vendor telemetry order-of-magnitude figures without published precise methodology. REFUTED items (for transparency): four claims failed 3-vote verification and must NOT be used — (1) the specific in-browser native-vs-browser slowdown ratios (16.9x CPU / 4.9x GPU PC, 15.8x/7.8x mobile) were refuted 0-3; (2) the specific Gemini Nano four-state user-activation framing was refuted 1-2; (3) PhishSnap's specific 0.79/0.76/0.78/0.82 metrics were refuted 0-3; (4) PhishSnap's pHash evadability-against-adaptive-layouts claim was refuted 0-3. Biggest gap: GAP D (local feedback capture + conformal calibration + single-user active learning) produced ZERO surviving claims — there is no verified evidence in this pass on rrweb session-replay capture for security events, decision-time feature-vector snapshot schemas, Transcend-style conformal prediction / credibility / p-values / drift detection, IndexedDB/unlimitedStorage corpus design, or offline threshold re-tuning and corpus replay. GAP D should be treated as unresearched and re-run.

## Open questions

- GAP D is entirely unanswered: what are concrete record schemas for decision-time feature-vector snapshots, and is rrweb (or a lighter capture) practical for reconstructing security events client-side within MV3 storage limits? What conformal-prediction / abstention design (Transcend-style credibility, p-values, drift detection) and active-learning strategy fit a single human's very small labeling budget, and how do you replay a local corpus to measure FP/TP deltas before shipping a threshold/weight change?
- What is the realistic per-inference latency and memory footprint for a SMALL security-relevant model (e.g. a logo-embedding or lightweight classifier) specifically inside an MV3 offscreen document on commodity hardware — the surviving sources give framework speedups and worst-case memory but not a concrete budget for the target model class?
- Which shipping browser extensions or security tools actually DETECT DoubleClickjacking and ClickFix at the interaction layer (not URL blocklist), and are there any published detection/false-positive rates for such client-side interaction monitors? The research established the gap but not the detector landscape or measured FP rates for interaction-level defenses.
- Can a logo-embedding model OR an on-device vision-language model (e.g. Gemini Nano multimodal) actually run client-side in an extension at an acceptable model size AND false-positive rate for visual phishing — i.e. closing the gap between Phishpedia's server-side 98.2% precision and PhishSnap's on-device-but-low-accuracy pHash floor?

## Refuted (transparency)

- "In-browser DL inference is substantially slower than native: averaging 16.9x slower on CPU and 4.9x slower on GPU on PC devices, and 15.8x (mobile CPU) / 7.8x (mobile GPU) on mobile, measured across 9 models on 50 PC + 20 mobile devices. This sets a hard latency-budget ceiling for any MV3-hosted on-device model." (vote 0-3, https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3688843)
- "Gemini Nano / Prompt API availability is gated behind four runtime states (unavailable, downloadable, downloading, available) and the model download is opt-in: it requires meaningful user interaction (user activation) before a session can be created, so it is not silently default-available even on supported hardware." (vote 1-2, https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/get-started)
- "The perceptual-hash (pHash) approach achieves only modest accuracy: 0.79 accuracy, 0.76 precision, 0.78 recall, 0.82 F1 on a 10,000-URL PhishTank/Netcraft 2024 dataset, indicating a low realistic accuracy floor for pure perceptual-hash visual phishing detection." (vote 0-3, https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02243v1)
- "Perceptual hashing is evadable against adaptive/novel layouts: PhishSnap misclassifies brandless phishing templates or adaptive designs that differ significantly from legitimate layouts, illustrating the evadability weakness of pHash versus logo-CNN/Siamese embedding methods." (vote 0-3, https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02243v1)
